ctx: The Lyst Index is a quarterly ranking of fashion’s hottest brands and products online. Its proprietary methodology combines demand data from 160million annual shoppers using the Lyst platform with a curated set of signals across social, search editorial, and emerging AI discovery channels. Brands are evaluated across three dimensions of data - Desire, Demand, and Discovery - capturing the full arc of how fashion attention forms, converts, and spreads online. The model prioritises aspiration-led demand, applies recency weighting, and excludes activity driven purely by discounting or negative attention, to track fashion brand heat over a three month period.

- Released second jewellery collection, with ‘Thorns’ campaign shot by photographer Guido Mocafino

The latest Lyst Index shows resort-ready labels dominating the rankings, warm-weather accessories topping the hottest products lists, and sport continuing to serve as both inspiration and investment for fashion shoppers worldwide. Across desire, demand and discovery signals, consumers increasingly gravitated towards brands that met the season in real time, capturing the mood of the moment as shoppers refreshed their wardrobes for summer.

Chanel retains its position at the top of the Index. The launch of its Coco Beach and Métiers d'Art 2026 collections have helped maintain brand discovery whilst searches on Lyst for Chanel sunglasses grew
Miu Miu climbs back into the top three, up two positions, after searches rose

quarter-on-quarter. Miu Miu's crochet bags and a hot New Balance collaboration, as seen on Coco Gauff at Wimbledon, all combined to propel the label up the rankings, demonstrating how cultural moments continue to accelerate search momentum and shopping intent. Dior once again completes the podium, while Burberry and Prada both climb up the hottest brands list.

Phoebe Philo makes its debut in The Lyst Index after searches for the label rose

quarter-on-quarter. The brand's expanded retail offering, combined with a number of seasonally relevant, product-led moments, have helped the label climb into the rankings for the first time, despite the relative restraint of its overall growth strategy. Phoebe Philo’s arrival reflects intense desire signals and cultural appetite from an in-the-know crowd, now translating into Lyst Index brand heat beyond its limited retail footprint.
Massimo Dutti rises the most places this quarter, climbing eight positions after searches for the brand rose
, fuelled by celebrity visibility during Cannes and growing demand for its elevated, Mediterranean-inspired wardrobe. Celine is the other major riser, climbing five places after searches rose

quarter-on-quarter, driven by a growing appetite for Michael Rider's directional offerings. Both brands maintained visibility across social and editorial conversations that continued to build momentum throughout the quarter.

Shoppers are refreshing their wardrobes in line with the season, finding new reasons to shop ahead of the autumn-winter investment pieces window. Cruise collections, resort dressing, and warm-weather accessories have all seen increased demand in Q2, with consumers showing a renewed appetite for romantic, vacation-ready styles. The strongest performers were the brands and products that remained highly discoverable throughout the quarter, surfacing naturally as shoppers searched for seasonal inspiration.
